capabilities: record and transcribe audio into Markdown notes
organize transcripts with an LLM into paragraphs, lists, or topic sections
mark terms, questions, highlights, and todos during recording
extract todo, people, and glossary candidates into daily notes
build topic pages from related notes with cited sources
disambiguation: Not a question-answering log despite the name; its main job is recording, transcribing, and organizing conversations into notes, with a Q&A tab as one sidebar feature.
extras: Manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. No backend, ads, analytics, or telemetry; API keys stored in Obsidian SecretStorage. Supports desktop and mobile; system audio capture on desktop needs a virtual audio device (VB-Cable, BlackHole, or PulseAudio/PipeWire). Extensive details on migration, backups, and crash recovery are covered in MAINTAINING.md, PRIVACY.md, and SECURITY.md.
intentEvidence: QnALog is derived from LexVoice, based on its last MIT-licensed release (2.1.2). It is independently maintained.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to record audio, transcribe it, and have an AI organize the conversation into structured, evidence-linked notes.

relations.evidence: QnALog is derived from LexVoice, based on its last MIT-licensed release (2.1.2).

summary: Voice recorder and transcription plugin that turns recorded conversations into structured Markdown notes using user-configured speech-to-text and LLM services.
